title: Definite Integrals
summary: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a), where F is an antiderivative. The constant C cancels. With a substitution, change the limits too.
As the limit of a sum: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = lim h→0 h[f(a) + f(a + h) + … + f(a + (n − 1)h)], with nh = b − a.
∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x)dx; ∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x)dx. ∫₋ₐᵃ f(x)dx = 2∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx if f is even, and 0 if f is odd. Split the integral where |…| changes sign.
Typical use: I = ∫₀^(π/2) cos³x/(sin³x + cos³x)dx. Replacing x by π/2 − x gives the same with sin and cos swapped; adding, 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.
Area under y = f(x) from a to b (f ≥ 0) = ∫ₐᵇ y dx. Area between two curves = ∫ₐᵇ (upper − lower) dx, with a and b the x-coordinates of the intersections.

mcq.work: Put t = x² + 1, dt = 2x dx: ½∫₁² dt/t = ½(log 2 − log 1) = ½ log 2.
The integrand changes sign when x → −x: it is odd, so the integral over [−a, a] is 0.
I = ∫ sin³x/(sin³x + cos³x) dx too (x → π/2 − x). Adding: 2I = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4.

mcq: The area bounded by y = x³, x = 0, x = 1 and y = 0 is —
objective: True or False: (a) ∫₂³ 3ˣ dx = 18. (b) ∫_(−½)^(½) cos x log((1 + x)/(1 − x)) dx = 1.

(a) False — [3ˣ/log 3]₂³ = (27 − 9)/log 3 = 18/log 3.
(b) False — cos x is even and log((1 + x)/(1 − x)) is odd, so the product is odd and the integral is 0.
True or False: (a) ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x)dx. (b) ∫₀² 3ˣ dx = 8/log 3.
vsa: Find the area of the region bounded by y = x² and y = 4.

or: Find the area enclosed by y = x² and y = x + 2.

sa: Evaluate ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x − cos x)/(1 + sin x cos x) dx.

Replace x by π/2 − x: I = ∫₀^(π/2) (cos x − sin x)/(1 + sin x cos x) dx = −I.
So 2I = 0 ⇒ I = 0.

I = ∫ √cos x/(√cos x + √sin x) dx. Replacing x by π/2 − x (which keeps the limits π/6, π/3) gives I = ∫ √sin x/(√sin x + √cos x) dx.
Adding: 2I = ∫_(π/6)^(π/3) dx = π/6 ⇒ I = π/12.
Prove that y² = 4x and x² = 4y divide the square bounded by x = 0, x = 4, y = 4 and y = 0 into three equal parts.

The curves meet at (0, 0) and (4, 4).
Middle part: ∫₀⁴ (2√x − x²/4)dx = [(4/3)x^(3/2) − x³/12]₀⁴ = 32/3 − 16/3 = 16/3.
Lower part (under x² = 4y): ∫₀⁴ x²/4 dx = 16/3.
Upper part = 16 − 16/3 − 16/3 = 16/3. All three are equal.
la: Evaluate ∫₂⁴ 2ˣ dx as the limit of a sum.

or: Find the area of the smaller region bounded by x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 and x/a + y/b = 1.

Quarter ellipse area = πab/4. Triangle under the line from (a, 0) to (0, b) has area ab/2.
Smaller region = πab/4 − ab/2 = (π − 2)ab/4.

la: Find the smaller area enclosed by the circle x² + y² = 4 and the line x + y = 2.

The line meets the circle at (2, 0) and (0, 2).
Area = ∫₀² [√(4 − x²) − (2 − x)]dx = [quarter circle] − [triangle] = π − 2.
